title: There's a Fake Island on the Map Where Lost Data Points Pile Up
hook: Data with the wrong coordinates all lands on a single dot in the middle of the Atlantic

open.title: An island appears on the map in a patch of ocean with no island at all
open.line: In the sea off West Africa there's a point with no island on it. Yet in map data, error records keep landing right there. Why?

summary: Latitude 0, longitude 0 is open ocean with no island, but data with missing coordinates piles up there, so it got the name Null Island. A weather buoy named Soul was moored at that spot too.

text: In the sea west of Africa, there's a point at latitude 0, longitude 0.
It's where the equator meets the prime meridian.
It's ocean, about 600 km south of the West African coast.
The water there is about 4940 m deep.

panels.text: Not a single island out there?

text: Yet map data often has error records stamped here.
Data with wrong coordinates ends up at 0, 0.
So people gave the point an island name.
Null Island, from null, meaning no value.
It began as a joke in 2008, and even got a website introducing the island nation.
Actually, something real was there too.
A weather buoy tied to the seafloor.
Buoys in the tropical Atlantic network were named after music genres.
In 2018, reports said fitness app records set to 0, 0 to hide a location showed up here too.
